name: AI incidents & governance
summary: The European Commission confirmed on 19 Nov it was hit by an AI-generated cyber campaign that took some systems offline
state: The European Commission confirmed on 19 Nov that it had been targeted by what its spokesperson called an AI-generated cyber campaign, detected on 22 Oct, and had temporarily taken several applications offline; most have been restored and it reported no evidence of a staff-wide data breach (The Star; Daily Sabah). This follows Google's report on 16 Nov of attackers using AI agents to find and exploit flaws without human input. A significant misuse incident keeps Watch; searches on 28 Nov found no confirmed AI-enabled attack on critical infrastructure.
for_you: Organisations face faster, more automated phishing and intrusion attempts. The UK's National Cyber Security Centre publishes guidance for businesses and individuals on protecting accounts and systems.
rubric_hit: Significant AI misuse incident (AI-driven attack on EU Commission, confirmed 19 Nov): Watch

sources.title: The Star — EU Commission confirms it was targeted in cyberattack through use of AI tools
Daily Sabah — EU confirms it was targeted in cyberattack through use of AI tools

why: Powerful AI systems are being deployed faster than safeguards; serious incidents or governance breakdowns carry systemic risk.
drivers: Model releases, misuse incidents, regulation, compute controls, deepfakes in elections.

rubric.alert: AI-enabled attack on critical infrastructure, or AI-attributed mass harm event.
rubric.watch: A significant AI misuse incident, major deepfake disruption, or regulatory confrontation.
rubric.normal: No serious AI-attributed harm events or governance shocks this week.
